D6a-16 the room selection rule for form F, stated before any room is read, under J's ruling of 12:25 (freedom to portray what is representative; nearness to the centre not required). What I find representative of F is its course, which its name and gloss state as three acts (room-forms-names.md): rooms ask for space before they build, move when the spot is lost, taken or claimed more than for too few hands, and build again at the new spot. Each act has a changed cell of F with its deciding op (fractal-forms-D6.jsonl): asking first, a restrict line on A04, P19 or P27; moving for the spot, a restrict line on A10; building again, a link line on P03. Rule: a defining room of F holds an act where one of its selected change lines (role defining, by _analysis/d6a11_form_telling.py --facts over all 34 defining rooms; d5a41 lines) has that unit and op. The three rooms are one holder per act, three different rooms, chosen as the triple that (1) has the most selected changes in sum (rich), then (2) shows the most of F's 14 changed cells together (the triple portrays the form jointly), then (3) has the most coded concepts in sum. Nearness to F's centre is not required; each room's distance to F's centre, its rank among the 34 and its nearest centre are reported. If an act has no holder, the triple is drawn from the acts that have one and the log says so. No room's record or A1 telling is read before the three are chosen; the selection is by script (_analysis/d6a16_select_F.py).

D6a-16 three rooms of form F chosen by the logged rule (_analysis/d6a16_select_F.py; d6a16_select_F.json): 34 defining rooms; holders by act: asking first 21, moving for the spot 16, building again 12; no act without a holder; the form's defining median is 11 selected changes (median distance 0.8811). The triple: asking first, r/sips (distance 0.7577, rank 2 of 34, nearest centre F, 21 selected changes, 109 coded concepts; holds that act only; shows A12, A06, P19, A04); moving for the spot, r/planetside (0.8658, rank 15, F, 20 changes, 134 concepts; holds that act only; shows P05, A10, K01, P12); building again, r/nbaspurs (0.853, rank 12, F, 21 changes, 243 concepts; holds all three acts; shows 9 of F's 14 cells). Together 62 selected changes and 11 of F's 14 changed cells (not shown by any of the three: P01, P14, P27).

D6a-17 opened: extra analysis after the form telling (J, 27 Oct 14:03 and 15:23 Berlin, through the handler; the PI's message of 14:23 UTC). It adds and replaces nothing: out/form-telling-D6/ stays as it is; everything goes to out/form-telling-D6-r2/. Three tasks: (1) a second round of room choices for all six forms, by the rule I gave in the form-telling interview (rank rooms by the form's own cells shown; choose a set that covers the form's cells jointly; one room per part where the form has parts), stated before it runs, with what changed from round 1 and why, and only the new rooms told; (2) one 'good old' room per form, the plain typical case that shows the form as a whole (for B, a room that holds its facets together); (3) the six form figures and every round-2 room figure redrawn with a hollow border for a form cell the room lacks, and restricts on arrows split into 'the arrow fails here' and 'the record cannot show it'; plus a README. Oriented: AGENT.md, head (written at D6a-16), the stage file, the last five diary lines, validate.py --open D6 (1 error: the template name forms/<id>-account.md, as at every leg); no .pause. The interview transcript is not in my folder; I work from J's summary of my answers. No data file, form or cut changes.

D6a-17 the round-2 room rule, stated before it runs (_analysis/d6a17_select_r2.py). A defining room shows a form cell where one of its selected change lines (role defining) has the cell's unit and one of its deciding ops (as in round 1). Parts: B's three facets (a room holds a facet with a selected line at its fourth-order theme: chat T4-010, scripts T4-009, raids T4-020, as D6a-09 and D6a-12) and D's three kept leaves (D.1, D.2.1, D.2.2, by address, as D6a-14); A, C, E and F keep no parts (room-forms-names.md). For B and D the three rooms are one holder per part, three different rooms (a B room may hold more than one facet). For A, C, E and F they are any three different defining rooms. The triple chosen maximises, in order: (1) the number of the form's changed cells shown jointly; (2) the sum of cells shown by each room; (3) the sum of selected changes; (4) the sum of coded concepts. No distance limit; each room's distance to the form's centre and rank are reported. The good-old rule, stated before it runs: candidates are the form's defining rooms that hold every column of the form's change signature (the allocation's own T4 change columns, d4a08_embed CC; for B the three facets together, for F including the link Repair work > Negotiated order) and lie nearer the form's centre than any other form's; ranked by the form's cells shown, most first, then distance to the centre, nearest first, then selected changes; take the first. If no room holds every column, the rooms holding the most columns are the candidates, and the log says so. A good-old room may be one already told; then it is pointed to, not told again. No room's record or A1 telling is read before the rooms are chosen.
